body:
An LSP trace is basically a log of the network traffic between the language server and the client. What you provided is correct 👍

So the issue is the following: Each editor can decide to give a language a different name (languageId). Those ids are only standardized for a few common languages, but GDScript is not one of those.

Kate seems to have assigned `godot` as language id for GDScript files. But our "canonical" language id is `gdscript`. This did not matter previously but starting with 4.6 the language server will only respond to specific language ids, since we had issues were we were trying to parse other languages like Rust as GDScript.

Ideally kate would modify it's configuration for GDScript files to `gdscript`.
We can add `godot` to our internal list for the time being though.

The error messages on Godot's side are a separate issues were we rely on an optional feature which Kate does not seem to support. Previously this would fail silently.

Ah, thank you for the clarification! Adding a file-type override seems to have resolved the major LSP issues in 4.6. ## Workaround Add a new `GDScript` entry in `Modes & Filetypes` under the `Open/Save` category in Kate's preferences. And set its priority to be higher than `Scripts/Godot`. Duplicate the LSP settings for `godot`, but change it to `gdscript` ## Result *It's usable again! albeit the flood of errors* https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/81d4707b-56d6-453c-be04-e7c6a6b9ca44
